transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-04 16:00 UTC | Duration: 42 mins
Attendees: Sana Patel (Redwood AE), Marco Li (Redwood SE), Jules Moreno (Product), Aisha Khan (OrionAI Head of ML), Ravi Menon (Infra), Laura Chen (PM)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): walked through model catalog, filtering open models by license and perf, drilled into the compat matrix, demoed Console route creation and Optimize suggestions. Agreed to run a small POC and exchange security docs.

[00:00] Sana: hey everyone, thanks for joining, can you all see my screen?
[00:07] Aisha: yes, looks good, hey Sana. we've got Ravi and Laura with me.
[00:12] Marco: great, i'll kick off with the model catalog -- quick note, sorry if the auto captions are wild, sometimes it says kv-cache as k v cat, etc.
[00:23] Marco: so here is the catalog view, by default we show curated open models, license type, and verified perf profile. you can filter on license, flop counts, memory, and hardware compatibility.
[00:37] Laura: are the perf profiles from your hosted runs or third-party benchmarks?
[00:42] Marco: mostly Redwood-hosted benchmarks across our infra matrix; we run each model on a set of instance shapes and sequence lengths, that's where the perf profiles come from. some community numbers are visible but flagged.
[00:55] Aisha: can you filter out anything that's non-commercial or that has a viral license?
[01:00] Marco: yep, there's a license filter. i'll toggle to show only permissive / commercial-friendly open models. now you see models like rw-llama-2-13b-q and a few smaller opt variants.
[01:12] Ravi: quick question on naming -- sometimes your product names are spelled Redwood Optimise in the docs i saw, is that the same as Optimize?
[01:18] Jules: same product, just spelling variants in older docs, apologies for confusion.
[01:22] [01:25] Marco: switching to compatibility matrix tab. this is important -- it maps model architecture, quantization format, supported kernels, and recommended GPU families. so for example, a 13B dense model quantized to 4-bit on Ampere has different kernel path than on Hopper.
[01:40] Marco: i can filter rows to show only models compatible with our Dedicated T4 pool, or filter by sequence length distribution.
[01:48] Laura: do you codify sequence length distributions per workload?
[01:52] Marco: we surface sample distributions; also Optimize suggests per-route batch sizes and KV cache heuristics based on sample traces.
[02:00] [02:03] Aisha: how accurate are your latency numbers in the catalog for short tail latencies? we care about p95 under 200ms.
[02:10] Marco: the perf profiles show median and p95 at several concurrency points. for p95 under 200ms we typically point to smaller quantized variants or enabling prefix caching. in hosted we also do pre-warm and warm pools.
[02:22] Ravi: what about tokenization differences, same tokenizer across your variants? we've hit tokenization drift between forked models before.
[02:29] Marco: tokenizer is model-specific but we annotate tokenizer family and byte-level compat. we also have a tokenizer validation suite you can run during POC.
[02:38] [02:40] Marco: switching to Console - creating a route is two clicks, pick model, pin version, set rollout to canary 10% or 100%, attach a cost cap or fallback route. nice for staged rollouts.
[02:52] Sana: for the demo i'll create a new route called orion-catalog-test and pick rw-llama-2-13b-q as an example.
[02:58] [03:05] Sana: set concurrency to 8, streaming enabled. Optimize is suggesting batch size 4 and quantization profile q4_0. that suggestion is based on your expected 90-token avg.
[03:20] Laura: can Optimize recommend when to fallback to a larger/smaller variant?
[03:24] Marco: yes, there are automatic fallback policies: cost-first, latency-first, or hybrid. based on runtime metrics it will switch to a compatible model variant. we keep the same API surface so app logic doesn't change.
[03:36] Aisha: curious about metrics retention and logs -- for compliance we need 90 days of request logs and audit.
[03:44] Jules: we have configurable retention, audit logs, and integrations with SIEMs. Private deployment supports customer-managed KMS and on-prem vaults for keying.
[03:55] [04:00] Ravi: network wise, for Private we need to allow only egress to certain subnets; does your installer support static egress IPs?
[04:07] Jules: yes, we can run in VPC with NATs or static IPs; we'll share the runbook.
[04:12] [04:15] Marco: back to the catalog -- here's the bench detail page: throughput, latency heatmaps per sequence length, kernel path notes, and the exact commit hash of the model repo used. we link to the benchmark notebook.
[04:30] Marco: note that some models have multi-kernel fallbacks; sometimes attention implementation falls back to slower kernel on long sequences. we annotate that.
[04:39] Laura: is the benchmark code open? can we rerun it in our infra?
[04:43] Marco: yes, we share a reproducible stack and a small harness; i'll attach links. (link: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/orion-sample)
[04:55] [05:00] Aisha: for the POC we want to evaluate 2 models for reranking and 1 model for chatbot. suggested metrics: p95 latency, tokens/sec cost, and quality via a small eval set.
[05:12] Sana: good, we'll propose a POC plan: 2-week run on Dedicated with a small traffic replay, run accuracy evals and perf profiling.
[05:20] Ravi: cost question: how does Dedicated pricing change with burst capacity?
[05:24] Jules: Dedicated is commit-based. burst is billed at a premium hourly rate; we can model different commit tiers. i'll include a sample TCO.
[05:34] [05:40] Marco: quick demo of Optimize's recommendation UI: you can upload a traffic trace (or paste sample), it will recommend dev-time flags: batch size, prefix cache keys, quant profile, and a suggested route config. it also estimates token cost delta and latency impact.
[05:56] Marco: watch this example: with q4_0 we get 35% cost reduction and ~10% latency increase on p50, p95 stays within target for that workload. the UI shows a sensitivity chart.
[06:10] Laura: can we pin models per route but have a global fallback?
[06:14] Marco: yes, route-level pinning plus global fallback is supported. we also do canary rollouts by region.
[06:20] [06:22] Aisha: security quick check - do you support SAML SSO and SCIM?
[06:26] Jules: yes SAML, SCIM, RBAC, and audit trails are supported; Private gets additional HSM/KMS integrations.
[06:34] Ravi: and in VPC mode do logs ever leave the customer network?
[06:38] Jules: in Private deployment, logs are customer-managed and can be routed to your SIEM; hosted will retain logs per retention policy but can export via subscriptions.
[06:47] [06:50] Sana: circling back - i'll summarize and then Marco will walk a couple of edge cases.
[06:55] Sana: next steps: we'll send pricing and the compatibility spreadsheet, and we want a traffic trace and eval prompts from you.
[07:05] [07:08] Marco: edge case one - very long sequences (2k+ tokens): many kernels slow down and some quant formats lose accuracy; we tag models that degrade beyond a threshold.
[07:20] Marco: edge case two - heavy multi-turn chat with KV cache churn: we suggest a hybrid caching strategy and pinning KV stores to avoid cold loads. sometimes the transcriptions call this k v cache as keev cache, so apologies for weird captions.
[07:38] Laura: if we want to run the POC in our cloud using your private control plane, what's the usual timeline for onboarding?
[07:45] Jules: typically 2-3 weeks to provision the private control plane, then a couple days to connect to your VPC and run initial tests. Dedicated can be faster if you want hosted capacity.
[07:55] [08:00] Aisha: any concerns about model licensing when we ship to customers?
[08:04] Marco: we flag models with restrictive licenses; our legal team maintains a license registry and we'll advise on suitable open models for commercial use.
[08:12] Ravi: can Optimize suggest tokenization fixes or normalization for consistent prompts?
[08:17] Marco: it highlights tokenization anomalies and can recommend prompt pre-processing steps; it's not a tokenizer rewrite but will flag drift.
[08:25] [08:30] Laura: can we export the compat matrix as CSV?
[08:33] Marco: yes, exportable CSV with columns for model, quant, supported kernels, recommended gpus, notes.
[08:40] [08:42] Sana: quick live test of the API - i'll send a single request via the Console playground to the orion-catalog-test route.
[08:48] Sana: request payload pasted. (short pause) response streaming... okay streaming looks fine, tokens arriving in chunks.
[08:58] Ravi: latency looks acceptable on this sample, but we'll provide a real trace.
[09:03] [09:05] Marco: one more note: we often recommend a two-model strategy for chat + rerank: smaller quantized model for rerank and a slightly larger for generation. routing rules can orchestrate that.
[09:20] Aisha: and monitoring — what dashboards will we get?
[09:25] Jules: per-route latency, token counts, cost per token, user-level error alerts, and model-regression alerts tied to your eval set.
[09:34] [09:38] Laura: let's talk about scheduling: we can aim to start POC week of 3/17 after we gather traces.
[09:44] Sana: perfect, we'll follow up with the doc pack.
[09:47] [09:50] Marco: i'll drop the compatibility spreadsheet link in the follow-up and include recommended quant profiles per model.
[09:56] Jules: i'll include the security/compliance checklist and runbook for Private.
[10:02] Sana: any remaining questions from Orion?
[10:06] Aisha: none for now, thanks.
[10:08] Ravi: no, thanks.
[10:10] Laura: all good.
[10:12] Sana: thanks everyone, we'll send the follow-ups by end of week.

End of transcript.

References shared: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/orion-sample , security checklist link: https://redwood.ai/docs/security-checklist (note: links may be redacted in final export).
